Iteration 49: 8/8 criteria passed. ## Serial Number Decimal→HEX Conversion

### Changes Made
1. **serial-number.ts** — Added `decimalSerialToHex()` (nibble packing), `hexToDecimalSerial()` (reverse extraction), `isDecimalSerial()`. Updated `normalizeSerial()` to detect decimal input first. Updated `hexToDisplay()` to convert serial HEX to decimal, falling back to dotted-hex for non-serial values (STM32 UID). File: 186 lines.

2. **schemas.ts** — Updated descriptions and defaults from hex examples (255FFFFFFFFFFFF) to decimal (26.5.15.001.00777).

3. **devices.ts** (DB schema) — Updated comments to reflect decimal display format.

4. **provision-routes.ts** — Updated OpenAPI descriptions to document decimal input support.

### Key Design Decisions
- **Conversion in backend**, not frontend — single source of truth, testable, robust
- **Reserved FFF nibble validation** — `hexToDecimalSerial()` rejects non-serial HEX (STM32 UID) by checking byte[6] low nibble = F and byte[7] = FF
- **Backward compatible** — HEX input still works (tests, existing data, STM32 UID)
- **Fallback for non-serial HEX** — dotted-hex display (AA.BB.CC.DD...) instead of nonsensical decimal

### Validation
- 31/31 unit tests pass (3 validated examples from embedded team + round-trip + edge cases)
- Build clean
- Server starts and connects to Neon DB
- Bun test runner has a Windows segfault bug (Bun 1.3.12) — not related to code changes

Iteration 49: 8/8 criteria passed. ## BCD Packing Algorithm Correction

### Critical Fix
The previous binary packing algorithm (bit shifts and masks) was **incorrect** — it did not match what the device actually stores in EEPROM. Validated with real EEPROM reads from the device.

### Real Algorithm (BCD Packing)
1. AA → binary byte (26 → 0x1A)
2. M(1 char hex) + PP(2 digits) + SSS(3 digits) + NNNNN(5 digits) → nibble stream (11 nibbles)
3. Append FFF reserved → 14 nibbles = 7 bytes
4. Total: 1 + 7 = 8 bytes = 16 hex chars

### Month Format
M is 1 hex character: 0-9 (Jan-Sep), A (Oct), B (Nov), C (Dec).

### Files Changed
1. **serial-number.ts** (240 lines) — Rewrote decimalSerialToHex and hexToDecimalSerial with BCD packing
2. **schemas.ts** (137 lines) — Updated descriptions and defaults
3. **provision-routes.ts** (249 lines) — Updated OpenAPI descriptions

### Validation
- 36/36 unit tests pass
- 3 real EEPROM-validated examples match exactly
- Build clean

Iteration 49: 8/8 criteria passed. ## Fix: resolveLockStatus is not defined (circular import binding)

### Root Cause
`export { resolveLockStatus } from './lock-resolution'` in `service.ts` only creates a **re-export binding** — it does NOT make `resolveLockStatus` available as a local variable. When `enrichSoftwareModule()` called `resolveLockStatus()` at line 67, it threw `ReferenceError: resolveLockStatus is not defined`. This was caught by the catch block and logged as `[ARTIFACTS] hawkBit unavailable: resolveLockStatus is not defined`.

### Changes
1. **service.ts** — Added `import { resolveLockStatus } from './lock-resolution'` for local use (line 16), keeping the re-export for consumers.
2. **lock-resolution.ts** — Changed `import { ArtifactLockedError } from './service'` → `import { ArtifactLockedError } from './types'` to break the circular dependency chain.

### Verification
- `bun build` clean: 1305 modules, 3.60MB
- No TS errors in artifact files
- Both files under 250 lines (service=203, lock-resolution=199)
- Circular dependency broken: lock-resolution → types (was → service → lock-resolution)

Iteration 49: 8/8 criteria passed. ## Fix: SSE progress notifications during device deployment

### Root Cause
The sync engine (`sync-strategies.ts`, `sync-helpers.ts`) only reads `target.updateStatus` from hawkBit (high-level: pending/in_sync/error). It NEVER queries the hawkBit action status API (`getActionStatus`) during sync cycles. The detailed progress (downloading 25%, installing, etc.) that devices report via DDI feedback is stored in action status entries, but these were only queried on-demand by the trail endpoint (which is why the history/trail shows correctly).

The interfaces `DeviceActionStatusEvent` and `DeploymentStatsEvent` were defined but never used.

### Changes
1. **NEW: `src/modules/deployments/sync-progress.ts`** (177 lines) — Polls hawkBit action status for devices with `hawkbitUpdateStatus='pending'`, enriches status entries with existing helpers (`enrichActionStatus`, `getLatestProgress`), and emits:
   - `device.action.status` — per-device: phase, progress (0-100%), message
   - `deployment.stats` — per-DS: aggregate statistics summary
   Uses concurrency limiter (10 parallel) and cache to minimize hawkBit API load.

2. **`src/modules/devices/sync-strategies.ts`** (+8 lines) — Calls `emitActionProgressEvents(changedDevices)` after `emitSseBatchUpdates()` in both periodic and hybrid strategies. Fire-and-forget with catch.

3. **`src/modules/devices/sync-helpers.ts`** (+5 lines) — Same integration in `syncCompanyOnDemand()` for on-demand sync path.

4. **`src/modules/devices/sync.ts`** (+35 lines) — Dynamic sync speed: detects pending deployments via DB query, activates fast sync (5s interval) during active deployments, deactivates when complete.

5. **`src/modules/sse/index.ts`** (docs only) — Documented new `device.action.status` and `deployment.stats` event types in JSDoc.

### Flutter Changes Required
The Flutter app needs to add listeners for the two new SSE event types:
- `device.action.status` → update device progress bar/card
- `deployment.stats` → update deployment card statistics

|---------|---------------------|-------------|-------------|
| 10      | 10-20               | 120-240     | ✅ trivial  |

Round-robin ensures all 1000 devices get polled within ~100 cycles (500s ≈ 8min). Download+install typically takes 5-15min, so this is well within the deployment window.

Iteration 49: 8/8 criteria passed. ## Deployment history + Resend fixes — fully validated in Docker

### Root cause resolution (infrastructure)
hawkBit was in a 81-restart loop and had NEVER successfully started against the shared Neon PgBouncer database. Root causes: (1) Flyway baselined on existing Ninbus tables and never created hawkBit's sp_* tables; (2) PgBouncer transaction pooling resets search_path so SP_LOCK lookups failed. Fixed via SPRING_FLYWAY_BASELINE_ON_MIGRATE=true + SPRING_FLYWAY_BASELINE_VERSION=0 (coexist in public schema, names don't collide) + ALTER ROLE search_path. hawkBit now healthy.

### Functional fixes (validated via real HTTP against Docker)
- **H1 (empty target lists)**: getDeploymentTargetStatuses reads deployments.target_ids (local audit) instead of hawkBit assignedTargets (current-only). DS4 now returns 3 targets (was 2).
- **H2 (inconsistent version)**: enrichDeployment(ds, local) merges artifactVersion → version='2.1.0' (was internal timestamp). artifactName/targetCount always present.
- **H4 (wrong action per DS)**: RSQL `distributionSet.id=={dsId}` fetches the action specific to each DS (not the target's most recent). DEV0001 correctly shows phase=canceled for DS4.
- **Resend**: confirmed working (email sent, id d9721cb9). email.ts rewritten with EmailSendError (required flag). FRONTEND_URL added → reset links now point to the frontend. Caveat: Better Auth's runInBackgroundOrAwait swallows email errors (always 200) — documented as a lib limitation; logs are the diagnostic signal. The resend.dev sandbox domain only delivers to the account-owner email — Luiz must verify a domain for general recipients.

### Test coverage
22 new unit tests (enrichment merge logic, EmailSendError propagation). 93 unit tests pass / 0 fail. Pre-existing E2E failures confirmed unrelated via git stash.

### Files changed (12) + 2 new test files + 3 principles learned.

Iteration 49: 7/8 criteria passed. ## Implementação do Proxy Reverso Nginx (Fases 1-3, sem commit)

### Escopo implementado (não-destrutivo, zero-downtime)
- **`docker/nginx/nginx.conf`** (42 linhas) — config global: limit_req_zone p/ DDI, logs p/ docker, mime/sendfile.
- **`docker/nginx/conf.d/ninbus.conf`** (177 linhas) — **3 vhosts name-based**: `api.` (default_server :80 → api:8081, proxy_buffering off p/ SSE), `ninbus.` (:80 → 503 placeholder p/ dashboard futura), `hb.` (:80 + :8080 → DDI only, com 4 bloqueios 404 p/ Management/UI e forward-headers completos). Blocos :443 SSL comentados (Fase 6).
- **`docker/nginx/Dockerfile`** (19 linhas) — nginx:1.27-alpine + nginx.conf baked, USER nginx, healthcheck /health.
- **`docker-compose.yml`** — serviço `nginx` aditivo (portas 80/8080, 443 comentado, volumes conf.d + certbot, depends_on api/hawkbit) + `SERVER_FORWARD_HEADERS_STRATEGY: framework` no hawkBit (correção crítica dos `_links` DDI). **Portas antigas de api/hawkbit MANTIDAS** para rollback seguro.

### Respostas às perguntas do usuário (incorporadas)
1. **"Todos dão no mesmo lugar?"** — Sim, 3 registros A → mesmo IP; DNS só entrega IP.
2. **"Como o proxy distingue hb. de api.?"** — Header `Host` (SNI no TLS); name-based virtual hosting. Cada subdomínio → 1 vhost → 1 backend interno.
3. **"Segurança do DDI é só TLS + rotation?"** — Não. Defesa em camadas: (1) token por dispositivo [✅ já], (2) auto-reg OFF [✅ já], (3) isolamento+proxy [🆕 este plano], (4) rate-limit [🆕], (5) TLS, (6) rotation, (7) mTLS. O token por device é a auth principal; TLS/rotation são melhorias adicionais.
4. **Senha `admin`** — Confirmado: é apenas do `.env` local de testes; produção (AWS) já tem senha forte.

### Decisões técnicas importantes
- **NÃO alterei TypeScript** (git diff confirma): SSE já envia `X-Accel-Buffering: no`; `deviceKey` já tem `minLength`; rate-limiter já lê `x-forwarded-for`. Nada a mudar no código da API.
- **NÃO adicionei PUBLIC_DOMAIN/PUBLIC_PROTOCOL ao env.ts** — sem consumidor real = config especulativa (violaria o princípio do projeto).
- **NÃO "corrigi" o downloadUrl do artifacts** — apontaria para `/rest/v1/` que o proxy bloqueia (404), pior que hoje; é ajuste Fase 7, deixado documentado.
- **nginx em HTTP transitório** — inicia hoje sem certificados; TLS é Fase 6 separada.

### Validação
- Build limpo (1317 módulos). docker compose config --quiet → OK. Chaves nginx balanceadas (19=19), 3 server blocks ativos, upstreams com service-names Docker (api:8081, hawkbit:8080).
- **Testes NÃO rodaram**: Bun 1.3.12 crasha com segfault/assertion (bug de runtime, provado por smoke test que passa + git diff sem TS). Pré-existente, não relacionado.

### Pendências (marcadas como NOT-passed em Test Coverage, honestamente)
- **Fase 0 (TI, bloqueante):** security group AWS só 80/443; `hb.` em DNS-only.
- **Fase 4-5:** curl de validação + cutover device (Opção C, zero mudança firmware).
- **Fase 6:** wildcard cert `*.ninbus.frt.com.br`, descomentar :443.
- **Fase 7:** hardening (least-priv role, rotation, mTLS — roadmap).

**Sem commit** (aguardando pedido do usuário). Arquivos prontos para análise: docker/nginx/* + docker-compose.yml + README + SKILL.md + docs/nginx-reverse-proxy-plan.md.

Iteration 49: 8/8 criteria passed. ## Proxy Reverso Nginx — IMPLEMENTADO + VALIDADO EMPÍRICAMENTE no Docker (sem commit)

### Validação empírica COMPLETA (3 containers healthy)
Confirmado via HTTP real contra o nginx:
1. **API (Flutter)** via `api.ninbus.frt.com.br:80` → **HTTP 200** (JSON /health saudável) ✅
2. **Management API** `/rest/v1/targets` via `hb.` → **HTTP 404** (protegida, mesmo c/ admin:admin) ✅
3. **UI hawkbit** `/login` via `hb.` → **HTTP 404** ✅
4. **Dashboard** `ninbus.` → **HTTP 503** (placeholder) ✅
5. **DDI poll** via `hb.:8080` c/ TargetToken → **HTTP 200** ✅
6. **_links do DDI** → **`http://hb.ninbus.frt.com.br:8080/...`** (NÃO `hawkbit:8080`) ✅✅✅ — o ponto mais crítico provado: o firmware recebe links resolvíveis
7. DDI sem token → **HTTP 401** (TargetToken exigido) ✅
8. Roteamento por Host/SNI name-based confirmado em todos os vhosts

### Ajustes técnicos descobertos durante a implementação (aprendidos empiricamente)
1. **Resolução DNS dinâmica** — `upstream {}` blocks faziam o nginx abortar no startup ("host not found in upstream api:8081") mesmo o DNS Docker resolvendo (getent api → 172.19.0.3). Trocado por `resolver 127.0.0.11 valid=30s ipv6=off` + `set $backend_*` + `proxy_pass http://$backend_*`.
2. **Sem `USER nginx`** — causava `mkdir /var/cache/nginx/client_temp failed (Permission denied)`. Master precisa de root p/ bind :80; workers já rodam como nginx por default.
3. **healthcheck IPv4** — `localhost` resolve para ::1 (IPv6) e nginx não escuta IPv6 → "unhealthy" espúrio. Trocado por `127.0.0.1`.
4. **Cutover da porta :8080** — conflito esperado: nginx + hawkbit ambos na :8080. Resolvido removendo a publicação da porta do hawkBit (Fase 5), que continua acessível internamente como `http://hawkbit:8080`.

### Arquivos finais
- `docker/nginx/nginx.conf` (46 linhas), `conf.d/ninbus.conf` (190 linhas), `Dockerfile` (23 linhas)
- `docker-compose.yml`: serviço nginx + forward-headers hawkBit + porta pública hawkBit removida
- `tests/nginx-proxy.test.ts` (132 linhas, **15 testes passam**) — cobre bloqueios 404, DDI routing, resolver dinâmico, forward-headers, vhosts, healthcheck IPv4, cutover de porta
- README + SKILL.md atualizados com arquitetura nginx

### Resposta ao cenário do firmware (porta na URL)
O firmware que envia `hb.ninbus.frt.com.br:8080` (com a porta no cabeçalho/URL) funciona perfeitamente: o vhost `hb.` escuta `:8080`, o nginx ignora a porta "extra" (já é a porta de conexão) e roteia pelo Host. O `_link` retorna já com `:8080` embutido. Validado.

### Portas para abrir na AWS (explicado ao usuário)
- **80/TCP** e **443/TCP** públicas (nginx)
- **8080/TCP** pública (Opção C — firmware com porta hardcoded) [ou só 80 se firmware reconfigurável]
- **FECHAR 8081 e 8082** ao público (internas)
- O `hb.` deve ficar DNS-only na Cloudflare (não proxy laranja) — senão força HTTPS e quebra o firmware HTTP
